items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: Yeah, I played violin with him, you know. I didn't stay with him long. And, uh, he had Willie Foster playing violin.

ctx.x: Yeah, I played violin with him, you know. I didn't stay with him long. And, uh, he had Willie Foster playing violin. That's George Foster's brother.
We got him up in Baton Rouge, remember Ralph?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Willie, Willie Foster, violin player, he told you all

ctx.x: And he had a good band. Uh huh. And them fellas, uh, Robichaux had a, what you call a reading band. Uh huh. All good musicians in his band. Sight readers. And, uh, uh, uh, when I was playing with, uh, with, uh, what you call him, uh, Joe Oliver, we playing at Hunts and Nagel on Ray's.

in Alverville, we used to buy that third grade music, we had a gate on the side of the door leading to the music stand and the Roe Show, he would, now that's what you call stealing, he'd come through that side door and come up and stick up on top by the music stand and when we'd be playing a new number he didn't know nothing about, he'd get over there and try to catch the title of it, you see, and if he'd get the title you'd see him writing down, he's gonna get that, and well we used to get some nice third grade…

Who Struck John? Did you ever hear that? Who? Who Struck John? Yeah. A friend of mine used to go up and listen to Joe, I hope I need to ask him the name of a number, he'd say, Who Struck John? Yeah. He'd ask him the name of the next number, he'd say, Who Struck John?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: he had Pop Foster's brother Willie Foster on the violin.

ctx.x: And you remember who else was in the band with Oliver when you worked with him and where

you played? Uh, let's see now. We played so many different, we was playing spot job. We didn't have no sound plays until we went to Hunson Nagel. Now, uh, let's see. What color was this, Hunson Nagel? He had, uh, Liberty in the Outerville. Liberty. He's band, he had, uh, uh, Call it the Casino. Oh yeah. He had, uh, Chris Kelly. Uh, no, uh, he had, uh, uh, Chris Miner on the drum. And he had, uh, uh, Alphonse Piku. And, uh, Joe Atkins. Uh, Joe Atkins. Uh. Joe Atkins. Uh. Joe Atkins. Ed Atkins. Ed Atkins was, yeah.…
That was the Magnolia band. Do you remember, uh, I think, uh, Louie Kepard tells me that he played in the Magnolia band too with Oliver for a while.
